definition: the components a grade is composed from, and how far the scoring of them has got

settled:
Trust is composite, and the worst part sets the letter.

Financial resiliency is the likelihood they keep operating, adjusted for exposure to mortgages, commercial real estate, AI shadow-loan derivatives and other stability factors.

Ethics is their record, measured by the scale of complaints and of legal fines for unethical practice.

Political ideology is a scale from Trumpist at nought to Enlightenment humanist at a hundred, a proxy for whether they will resist authoritarian pressure.

Ownership structure matters and is not yet scored. Mutual, cooperative, purpose-trust or employee ownership lowers capture risk. Being publicly traded introduces it by default.

I evaluate candidates with an AI research prompt scoring the first three from nought to a hundred, first run on the six largest US banks. It is a first draft. Scores do not yet map to a letter, so the letters are qualitative judgements, and worst-part-wins is how they work in practice rather than a written rule.

title: What A Trust Grade Is Made Of
